author: BBC News
description:
For the first time since World War Two, a far-right party has made a significant win in Germany, taking almost 44% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt. The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which has been labelled as “right-wing extremist” by domestic intelligence, is leading the national polls. 
 
Among its pledges at a state level are to defund “anti-German" art and teach children less about Hitler, as part of a “patriotism” agenda. 
 
This idea challenges the deeply held and decades-long German memory culture that insists people must never forget the Nazis’ crimes. 
 
The AfD describes German memory culture in its manifesto as a "guilt complex". BBC Berlin correspondent Jessica Parker talks us through the complexities of remembering Germany’s past, and the controversial ways in which the AfD wants to shape its future.

author: BBC News
description:
US President, Donald Trump, has said he will offer every adult American $5,000 (£3,700) if the Republican party wins the midterms.

President Trump gave no detail on how it would work or how he would fund it. Speaking at the party's first-ever convention in the middle of a US presidential term. He also said that the country’s war with Iran would not end until after the midterms. James is joined by Caitriona Perry and Faisal Islam to unpack these latest statements.

Plus, is there a more than 10% chance AI could kill all humans within a decade? The ‘Godfather of AI’ Geoffrey Hinton says this estimate by some experts isn’t an unreasonable one. The BBC’s Cyber Correspondent Joe Tidy is in the studio to tell us what people working inside AI have to say about the risks associated with it.

description:
US President Donald Trump said he would offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress in November's midterm elections – a plan that would cost more than a trillion dollars.
 
The offer was made in a speech at the party's first-ever convention in the middle of a US presidential term.
 
He gave no details on how it would work or be funded – saying only that the money would have to be spent in the US. Vice-President JD Vance has linked the plan to the revenue that Trump has raised from US tariffs on imported goods.
 
Democrats labelled it an "empty promise" and others questioned whether such a pledge was legal or feasible.

author: BBC News
description:
Doors have opened to the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition at the British Museum in London. 
 
It has gone on public display in the UK for the first time since it was created nearly 1,000 years ago. 
 
The 70m tapestry, originally embroidered in England but kept for centuries in France, tells the story of the Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
 
Outside the museum, visitors have queued to get in to be some of the first to see it.

author: BBC News
description:
It’s almost 20 years since the first iPhone was released and since then more than three billion have sold worldwide, and Apple has now unveiled its first ever foldable iPhone. 
 
With a book-style format, the new iPhone, dubbed the Duo, is the largest ever size of the product. And with a US starting price of $1,999 (£1,475) going up to $3,200, it is also the most expensive. UK prices start at £1,999.
 
Apple's new chief executive John Ternus said the Duo was "inspired by the iPad" but called the folding features "fluid and completely intuitive."

description:
At least five people are dead and 86 remain unaccounted for after a fire broke out on a ferry in the Philippines, the country's coastguard says.

Coastguard Captain Noemi Cayabyab says 43 people were rescued.

The fire engulfed the MV June Aster as it was taking 134 passengers and crew to Coron - a place popular with tourists.
